Thanks for the demo last week — MedFrame's clinical integrations team is ready to move into a short pilot but procurement and our security team have a couple of gating asks before we sign the pilot SOW. Two items in particular: 1) a signed attestation that data sent to Redwood will not be used to train or improve public models (no-training/no-derivatives commitment), and 2) a clear, repeatable export path for tenant artifacts and logs (we need to know how we can extract prompts/responses and clinical annotations at termination).

Can you also provide the latest SOC 2 report and a current subprocessor inventory or confirmation that any subprocessors storing EU data are EU-resident? Our legal team will need those with the attestation.

I've attached MedFrame_DPA_Annex.pdf (annotated) with the clauses we're prioritizing. Looking forward to a quick plan so procurement can proceed.

Hi all,

Short answer: yes, we can support both options. Details below for the SFTP path (preferred for onboarding because it provides a deterministic export artifact).

SFTP nightly export (what we propose):
- Delivery: daily encrypted tar.gz pushed to customer SFTP. File naming: medframe-yyyyMMdd-tenant123.tar.gz.gpg
- Encryption: AES-256 symmetric; we can also support GPG with customer public key for end-to-end.
- Auth: SSH key-based auth (per-tenant key pair). We support automated key rotation on a 90-day cadence; customer can request manual rotation.
- Retention: Redwood will retain a copy of the exported bundle for 7 days post-delivery to allow re-delivery in case of transfer issues. After 7 days the bundle is deleted from our staging cache.
- SLA: exports executed 02:00 UTC daily; we can provide a delivery success webhook/receipt.
- Onshore routing: we can land the export from EU-resident hosts (Frankfurt region) and avoid cross-border subprocessors if MedFrame requires EU residency.

API push option (alternate):
- We can push a per-interaction payload to a customer endpoint with TTL=24h or TTL=0 (ephemeral) depending on contract. Payloads can be encrypted with customer-managed KMS and mutual TLS. This is lower-latency but less convenient for bulk archival.

Attachments: sftp_config.txt (examples of hostnames, port, delivery path, and sample key rotation steps).

Let me know if you want a narrow checklist we can give procurement to sign off on (handshake steps, test delivery, acceptance criteria).

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
